newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Drugs boost Swedish shares in light trade.
newsitem.headline: Drugs boost Swedish shares in light trade.

text.p: Swedish shares reversed early losses and were higher at midday Tuesday with support from drugs stocks and rises on other European bourses as the dollar strengthened against the mark.
The Stockholm general index was 0.23 percent higher at 2,992.69 at 1030 GMT in fairly light turnover worth 1.94 billion crowns.
But brokers said there was no strong market direction.
"It feels as if there could be room for a rebound downwards but, on the other hand, it seems rather strong right now," said one broker.

The drugs sector was the best performer with the index rising 1.01 percent. Pharmacia & Upjohn rose five crowns to 266 after gains in New York overnight. Fellow drugs company Astra edged up 1.5 to 145.5 crowns.
Another winner in morning trade was car safety equipment maker Autoliv that gained 5.5 to 303 crowns. It also rose on Wall Street overnight.
One broker said index related funds were rumoured to have been selling Autoliv in recent weeks, depressing the stock, but this selling had now dried up.
Vehicle maker Volvo was flat at 207 crowns.
Its truck division raised its forecast for the total truck sales in the North American market to 200,000 in 1997 from 188,000.
"This is the second time that we have raised our forecast for the North American market this year," said company spokesman Stefan Lorentzson.
